questions.question: What is a distinguishing feature of a doubly linked list compared to a singly linked list?

options.text: Nodes have a pointer to the next node only
Nodes have pointers to both the next and the previous nodes
Nodes contain an additional field for data
Traversal is only forward

questions.question: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the beginning of a doubly linked list?

options.text: O(n)
O(log n)
O(n log n)

questions.question: Which operation is easier in a doubly linked list compared to a singly linked list?

options.text: Traversal from the head to the tail
Insertion at the head
Accessing the middle element by index
Deletion of a node when given a pointer to it

questions.question: What happens to the pointers when a node is deleted in a doubly linked list?

options.text: All nodes are shifted to fill the gap
Only the next pointer of the previous node is updated
Both the next pointer of the previous node and the previous pointer of the next node are updated
A new node is created to replace it

questions.question: What is the time complexity of searching for an element in an unsorted doubly linked list?

options.text: O(n)
O(log n)
O(n log n)
